name: Partholón

attributes.attribute: the least significant of the invaders
fought the Fomorians in a magical battle

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Partholon is an Irish hero. The Book of Invasions also calls him Partholon, Parthalan, and Parthanan. He was the least significant of the invaders. He came after Cesair and before Nemed. Medieval historians may have invented his name from Bartholomaeus. Partholon came to Ireland from Greece. He had killed both his parents. He lost his left eye as punishment. Thirty years after the great flood, he arrived with his people. They fought the Fomorians in a magical battle without blood. His wife Dealgnaid slept with the servant Togda while he was away.

okr.objective: Describe Partholon, leader of the Partholonians in Ireland.
key_results: Partholon came to Ireland from Greece after the great flood.
He fought off the Fomorians and led his people into Ireland.
His name may come from the figure Bartholomaeus.
